run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:11:11Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is caused by sparse but sustained HTTP 503 responses at frontend-proxy: its cumulative STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counter rose from 424 to 444 on span_name=ingress between 23:42 and 00:20 (while the 'router frontend egress' ERROR counter stayed flat at 396), an increase of 20 error spans, i.e. about 0.012/s, which is the same scale as the alert's reported 0.0111. Every 4xx/5xx access-log line readable for frontend-proxy (20 lines, 23:47:04-00:14:50) is identical in kind: HTTP 503, response flag UC, response-code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, UPSTREAM_CLUSTER frontend, UPSTREAM_HOST 100.71.53.109:8080 - the ClusterIP of the otel-demo frontend Service. The requests are spread over /api/products/*, /api/data, /api/cart, /api/recommendations and /. The frontend service itself records no new error spans (its ERROR counter stays at 1614), its pod is Ready with restartCount 0, and it produced no readable application logs, so the failure is at the proxy->frontend connection level rather than an error response returned by the frontend application; why the connection is terminated before a response could not be observed (traces stop at 23:44:29, no HTTP status metric exists, Envoy config is baked into the image). The only configuration-level fault-injection style setting found switched on is loadGeneratorFloodHomepage='on' (value 100) in ConfigMap flagd-config, but it is not temporally tied to the error rate and remains a hypothesis, not a confirmed cause. No Kubernetes object was observed applying the fault, so no root cause is named.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's cumulative STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counter for span_name=ingress rose from 424 (23:42) to 444 (00:20); span_name='router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR stayed constant at 396. Total frontend-proxy error spans were 820 at 23:41 and 840 from 00:16 to 00:21, so the increase in the sampled window is 20 ingress error spans.

In the readable frontend-proxy log range (23:31:00 through 00:15:57, with reads through 23:59:10 and 00:15:57), all 20 lines with a 4xx/5xx response are HTTP 503 with response flag UC and response-code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, UPSTREAM_CLUSTER 'frontend', UPSTREAM_HOST '100.71.53.109:8080', e.g. 23:47:04.642 GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM, 00:01:00.653 GET /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z, 00:14:50.650 GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM.

The 503 paths observed are spread across routes: /api/products/{id} (7 lines), /api/data/?contextKeys=... (4), /api/recommendations?productIds=... (2), /api/cart (1) and / (1), plus one more /api/products and one more /api/data line at 23:55 - i.e. no single route dominates.

100.71.53.109 is the ClusterIP of Service frontend in otel-demo (port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend); its only endpoint is 100.96.2.93, pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2, port 8080. So the 503s are resets on the proxy's connection to the frontend Service endpoint.

The observed error rate matches the alert's number: 20 503 responses between 23:47:04 and 00:14:50 is about 0.012 errors/s, comparable to the alert's 'current: 0.01111111111111111'; over the same period frontend-proxy span_name=ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET increased ~49,565 per hour versus ~20.3 for STATUS_CODE_ERROR (increase over 1h at 00:20:41), i.e. the error share is well under 1 percent of proxy spans.

The frontend service produced no new error spans during the sampled window: its STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter stayed at 1614 from 23:41 to 00:21. Same for accounting (1) and payment (4). Only frontend-proxy (+20), ad (39->43), fraud-detection (1->5) and recommendation (1->5) error counters increased, the latter three only a few per 40 minutes.

All 21 otel-demo pods are phase Running, containers ready and restartCount 0, including frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth (container started 2026-11-17T23:30:14Z) and frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 (started 23:30:14Z); no container has a lastState termination.

The only otel-demo events inside the window are a load-generator rollout at 00:02:01-00:02:02 (ReplicaSet load-generator-57ffcd644 SuccessfulDelete 'Deleted pod: load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89', ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd SuccessfulCreate, Pod load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, Deployment load-generator ScalingReplicaSet 0->1 and 1->0). No OOMKilled, Evicted, Failed or Unhealthy pod events appear.

Deployment load-generator is at revision 2 with env LOCUST_HOST=http://frontend-proxy:8080, LOCUST_USERS=50, LOCUST_SPAWN_RATE=5, LOCUST_AUTOSTART=true; Deployment flagd is at revision 2 running flagd v0.12.8 with command '/flagd-build start ... --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json'; Deployment frontend-proxy is at revision 1.

ConfigMap flagd-config (namespace otel-demo, key demo.flagd.json) contains flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage with state ENABLED, defaultVariant 'on' and variants {off:0, on:100}, description 'Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests.' Every other flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'.

The frontend container is CPU-throttled: throttled CFS periods / total periods is 0.22-0.31 over 23:50-00:20 with limits cpu=100m, memory=200Mi (requests cpu=50m, memory=100Mi); its working set rose from 240.9 MB (23:40) to 263.6 MB (00:20). frontend-proxy stays at ~41 MB working set with throttle ratio 0.04-0.06 (limits cpu=30m, memory=50Mi).
All 5 cluster nodes report Ready=True (KubeletReady) with MemoryPressure=False and DiskPressure=False.

Jaeger returned no trace data covering the 503 interval: the traces_search for frontend-proxy (window ending 00:21:02) returned traces whose newest span starts 2026-11-17T23:44:29.176 and source_end_at 23:44:29.175666, i.e. the last available traces precede the first observed 503 at 23:47:04.

Span-metric samples only start around 23:40-23:45: a 10-minute increase of frontend-proxy span calls is 6,030 at 23:45 and 12,790 at 23:50, and a 18:00-00:21 query reports source_start_at 23:45:00, so no baseline exists before ~23:45 (the cumulative counters already read 820 error spans at 23:41).

The full metric inventory of this Prometheus is 63 names; the only request/span telemetry series are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket. No http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_* or app_* series exist here: the query {__name__=~'.*request.*'} returned only the two kube cpu/memory request recording rules, and {__name__=~'app_.*|traces_.*'} returned only the two traces_span_metrics series.

The 503s are connection-level failures on the frontend-proxy -> frontend hop rather than application error responses: Envoy reports upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} for the 'frontend' cluster (no response received, UPSTREAM_SERVICE_TIME '-'), while the frontend records no error spans and logs nothing. The most plausible mechanism is the upstream frontend closing a pooled HTTP connection before it responds (e.g. an idle keep-alive connection being reused as the server closes it), which the proxy then reports as 503 UC.

Frontend CPU starvation may contribute: the frontend container is throttled in 22-31% of CFS periods under a 100m CPU limit while it serves ~14-24 proxy requests per second, which could make it slow to accept/handle connections on the proxy's upstream. This is unproven: throttling is continuous and flat while the 503s are sparse, and the frontend's own error counter never moved.

The fault-injection style flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage is switched on ('on' = 100) in ConfigMap flagd-config and its description says it floods the frontend with a large amount of requests; since the load generator's target is http://frontend-proxy:8080 and the proxy's upstream (frontend) is CPU-limited, an active flood could be driving the connection resets. This is not established: the 503 rate (~1 per 1.5 min) is unchanged across the load-generator rollout at 00:02:01 and 503s already existed at 23:47 before it, and the time the flag was switched on cannot be determined.

frontend-proxy pod damage or resource exhaustion is not the cause: its pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, no lastState termination, no OOMKilled/Evicted events, memory steady at ~41 MB, CPU throttle only 4-6%, Service frontend-proxy has one healthy endpoint, and there are no NetworkPolicies in otel-demo.

Failures of the frontend's own downstream services do not explain these 503s: the 503s are spread across routes whose backends differ (/api/products, /api/data, /api/cart, /api/recommendations, /), and the frontend service records zero new error spans throughout the window even though ad, fraud-detection and recommendation each accumulate only a handful of error spans per 40 minutes.

Node and cluster level health does not support a node-caused failure: all 5 nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure=False and DiskPressure=False, and all otel-demo pods are Running and ready with zero restarts.

Human follow-up: inspect the Envoy (frontend-proxy) upstream HTTP settings baked into the image - connection-pool idle_timeout / keep-alive reuse against the frontend's Node keepAliveTimeout - and align them or add retries/HTTP-2 toward the frontend cluster to eliminate the sporadic upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} 503s.

Human follow-up: make the failure observable - add an HTTP status-code metric for frontend/frontend-proxy (the only span-status series here are traces_span_metrics_*), restore trace export after 23:44:29, and enable application logging on the frontend container (it emitted no readable stdout/stderr in the sampled window).

Human follow-up: review whether RequestErrorRate should fire at a strictly-positive threshold; the metric here is roughly 0.011 errors/s (about one 503 per 90 s) against ~20-24 proxy spans/s, so a >0 threshold fires on sparse background errors.

gaps: No trace data exists for the 503 interval: Jaeger's newest returned trace starts 2026-11-17T23:44:29, so the failing requests (first 503 at 23:47:04) cannot be inspected span-by-span.

No change history is available (change_history is not integrated), so when the flagd flags in ConfigMap flagd-config were set (including loadGeneratorFloodHomepage='on') and why Deployment load-generator was rolled at 00:02:01 cannot be determined.

Prometheus samples for traces_span_metrics start around 23:40-23:45 and the counters already read 820 frontend-proxy error spans at 23:41, so there is no baseline to say whether ~0.011 errors/s is elevated; the 424 ingress and 396 egress error spans accumulated before 23:42 are also not readable in logs or traces.

The alerting rule's exact expression and metric are unknown: list_prometheus_rules returned nothing for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and nothing for type=alert, and no HTTP-status metric exists in this Prometheus, so the reported 0.0111 was only matched numerically to the span error rate.

The frontend container produced no readable stdout/stderr in the queried window (0 bytes read for 23:59:00-00:02:30), so the application-side reason for terminating connections could not be verified; the frontend's own error counter also shows no new error spans.
frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration is baked into the image (no ConfigMap/volume for it), so upstream idle/keep-alive timeouts, retry policy and fault filters could not be read or verified.

frontend-proxy logs outside the readable range (before 23:47:04 and after 00:15:57) were not available within the 4 MiB read limit, so the earlier error burst and any errors after 00:15:57 are unseen.
The ResourceQuota query in this cluster returned no objects (empty result), so quota limits are unchecked rather than proven absent.
It is unknown whether loadGeneratorFloodHomepage was in effect (value 'on'=100) during the 503 interval; the current ConfigMap content is the only flag state observed.
next_steps: Compare frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream connection-pool idle_timeout / keep-alive settings with the frontend Node server's keepAliveTimeout and headersTimeout, and align or retry on 503 UC.
Add HTTP status-code request metrics (server/client, by status) for frontend and frontend-proxy so that 4xx/5xx rates are directly measurable and alertable.
Repair trace export so Jaeger holds traces after 23:44:29, then inspect a failing ingress 503 trace once captured.
Confirm with the demo owner whether the loadGeneratorFloodHomepage fault flag is intentionally enabled; if not, switch it back to 'off' and observe whether the 503 rate changes.
Consider whether the RequestErrorRate alert should use a ratio and a non-zero threshold, given the observed rate of about one 503 per 90 seconds against ~20+ spans/s.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
